newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end down as cash slides.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end down as cash slides.

text.p: Sliding cash cattle prices weighed on CME live cattle futures, dragging them to lower closes, while feeder cattle ended lower in response to higher CBOT corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.075 to 0.450 cent per lb lower with June off 0.225 at 64.175 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.675 to 0.150 lower with August off most at 77.150 cents.

Cash cattle sold at $64 per cwt Tuesday in active trade. The price was down from last week's top price at some point during the day, packers lowered bid to $63 which kept pressure on most live cattle futures months, traders said. Rolling of longs from June into August supported the latter into the close, traders said.

Packers appeared to have adequate live supplies and available contracted cattle will likely keep bids for fed cattle working lower. They may also be pulling back on bids due to lighter-than-expected demand for beef, especially since wet and cool weather is limiting grilling, traders added.
Boxed beef values were quoted $0.11 to $0.43 per cwt lower at midday and the $64 cattle sales were the lowest since February.
Cargill Investor Services and Prudential Securities actively spread long August/short June, traders said.
Also, E.D.&F. Man sold August, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commercials bought the October 68 strangle. Liquidation continued in the June 64 strike. August volatility was steady to firm, pit sources added.

The higher trending CBOT corn futures and losses in deferred live cattle futures continued to weigh on feeder cattle. Technical fund selling adding to pressue and touched off sell stops that took August down to two week lows before short covering developed, traders said.
"The market is turning technically weak," one trader said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.05 to $77.42 per cwt.

LIT division of First Options, Rosenthal Collins and ABN Chicogo Corp sold early with ADM Investor Services, Rand Financials and Dean Witter sellers on the setback. Cargill bought on the scale down and also spread long August feeders/short February live cattle, pit sources said.
